game.name: Star Trek: Voyager - Across the Unknown

items.text: Greetings, Captains!
Patch 2.2 brings the Delta Chronicles 2 DLC with five new side missions, two new heroes and new ships to fight. Q Trials and the campaign get new options, balancing and a list of fixes.
Five new side missions: The Swarm, The Q and the Grey, Tinker Tenor Doctor Spy, Nightingale and Q2.
The Swarm: A race against time triggered by a distress signal from a solitary survivor trapped deep inside the territory of a highly hostile alien species known as the Swarm.

The Q and the Grey: The Q Continuum fractures into a destructive civil war between status quo and change, threatening an entire sector of the Delta Quadrant. Q proposes a shocking resolution: creating a new Q offspring with Captain Janeway!

Tinker Tenor Doctor Spy: The Doctor’s vivid daydreams spill out of control. Timing couldn't be worse: an eavesdropping alien species, the Hierarchy, hacks his daydreams, taking his alter-ego - the "Emergency Command Hologram" - for reality.

Nightingale: Harry Kim finally gets his moment in the Captain's chair when Voyager intervenes in a conflict between the Kraylor and the powerful Annari. Players can choose to let Harry prove himself as Captain - or assign the experienced Chakotay to handle the crisis.

Q2: Janeway's godmother skills are put to the ultimate test when Q leaves his rebellious, arrogant teenage son, Q Junior, in her care. Voyager must endure Junior’s chaotic pranks while teaching him discipline before the Continuum hands down a harsh punishment.

Q Logs: Alongside Tom and Tuvok, Q now also records his own log entries, offering commentary on the adventures of Voyager as well as his own family drama - featuring voice-overs in both English and German.
2 new heroes: Q and Phlox, each with their own combat abilities and their own dialogue and ending pop-up in Endgame. Phlox can also be unlocked as a hero reward in Q Trials.
New NPC ships: The Nightingale, the Annari Warship, the Hierarchy Assault Vessel and the Swarm ships.
New technologies: The Nightingale side mission allows the player to obtain the "Kraylor Cloaking Matrix," while The Swarm offers a chance to acquire the new "EMP Component" technology.
The Delta Chronicles 2 DLC is required to play the new missions, to read the new Q logs and to recruit Q and Phlox.
No repeated goals: You never get the same sector goal twice in a row now.
Auto-combat: The auto-combat screen now shows the same enemy combat power as the combat preparation screen.
Leave Sector: The Leave Sector screen updates now when you toggle the bonus distance.
Heroes: Janeway and Ransom are now survivalists.
Vidiian space: More variety in Vidiian combats.
Settings: A new option turns tutorial popups off.
Crew conditions: Events no longer announce hero conditions that can't be applied.
Rations: The Rations ship quest and the Dissatisfaction event now accept all high-tier food rations, including replicator rations.
Cold Fire: The quest tracker now explains how to assign a named hero to a room for several cycles.
Hunters Due: Reward events now tell you when a hero is injured, severely injured or left behind.
Uprising: Declining to resettle the ex-Borg no longer shows the 30 ex-Borg requirement.
Loyalties: Added a missing dialogue node and text.
Dissatisfaction: Removed an outdated condition from the second choice event.
Dialogue option Add Shuttles: The text is fixed, and the shuttlebay updates when shuttles are added.
Tech names now show correctly in dialogue options that require a tech.
Fixed an unexplained +1 in combat power.
Torpedoes and hero abilities can no longer be used during the combat victory screen.
You can no longer give input between the loading screen and the first cutscene, for example by focusing the resource bar.
Removed a stray apostrophe from the Natural Foods tutorial text.
See you in the Delta Quadrant, Captains!
gameXcite & Daedalic Entertainment
Greetings, Captains!

Patch 2.1 brings a brand-new game mode, Q Trials, and the Equinox DLC. The campaign gets new ship events, Delta Flyer options in three missions, balancing for the ship's economy and a long list of fixes.
New Game Mode: Q Trials

Q has a new game mode for you: bring your ship home through procedurally generated sectors, run after run. Q Trials has its own entry in the main menu, next to “New Campaign”, with additional save slots.

Choose your ship, your captain and your starting heroes. The captain grants a passive bonus, and one of 30 crew members can take the chair, from Janeway and Chakotay to Seven of Nine, Kes, Icheb and Seska. Your captain stays on the bridge and doesn't join PoI missions.

Q Modifiers: rule-bending run modifiers such as "Full House" (all quarters have 100% increased crew capacity, but each cycle has a chance that some crew get sick) or "Glass Cannon" (increases the ship's damage by 50% but reduces shield capacity and maximum hull integrity by 20%). At fixed distance milestones you’ll need to choose one of three - with the effects stacking up.
Q Challenges: raise the difficulty step by step. Every challenge level keeps all the lower ones active.

Every run is different. Sectors are generated from sector types, each with its own missions, PoIs, events, battles and music: Kazon space with Relora, Ogla and the Nistrim, the Krowtonan Guard, the Hirogen Hunting Grounds, Borg, Hazari, Vidiian and Devore space, trade and repair stations, slipstream and geodesic folds, plus night, nebula and ruined sectors. You never visit the same type of sector twice in a row.
Light years to home: instead of a fixed amount of sectors, your progress is counted in light years. Goals, rewards, resources, phenomena and enemies grow with the distance you've travelled.

Sector goals and exits: each sector has a main goal with several ways out (e.g. the more resources you gather, the further you can travel) and optional goals that work as shortcuts (e.g. finding a wormhole or building a slipstream drive).
Threat and factions: threat levels drive random encounters, and factions such as the Kazon remember what you did.
Familiar stories, new twists: PoIs and ship events from the campaign return in new variants, and homesickness follows the crew through the whole run.
Harvesting: send heroes away on shuttles to gather resources over time.
Heroes on missions: assign heroes to PoI events. Their attributes change the odds, and they gain experience, can be injured and need rest when fatigued.
Rewards after each sector: unlock a hero or tech permanently for future runs, or take resources, hull repairs and morale. Special exits give you two picks.
Meta progression: Tech that has been researched will stay permanent, but that progress will only be saved when jumping to the next sector.
Three Q Trials profiles with separate progression, and a Restart Run button.
Q introduces your trials in new cutscenes and comments on your results, with voice-over in English (by John de Lancie himself) and German.
New sector-jump cutscenes, loading screens that dynamically show your distance from home, a run summary with statistics, and tutorials for the new systems.
Q Trials save automatically after each PoI. Manual saves and sector saves aren't available in this mode.
Achievements can't be earned in Q Trials.
Take command of the U.S.S. Equinox in Q Trials and fight your way home against all odds. It's the ultimate challenge for experienced captains.

New playable ship (for Q Trials mode): the U.S.S. Equinox, with its own layout and rooms: bridge, main engineering, mess hall, sickbay, transporter room, bio lab, shuttlebay, Waverider shuttle bay and torpedo launch bays.
3 new heroes: Rudolph Ransom, Maxwell Burke and Noah Lessing.
New story mission: Spirits of Good Fortune, available in Q Trials with the U.S.S. Equinox.
A dark shortcut: the U.S.S: Equinox's bio lab can produce Crystalline Nucleogenic Compounds, fuel for a much longer jump across the stars… at a terrible cost.
The Equinox DLC is required to play as the U.S.S. Equinox and to recruit its heroes.

New ship events: Unauthorized Update, Critical Baryon Accumulation and Warp Core Damage. Events can now damage the warp core or a random room. Critical Baryon Accumulation slows the ship and injures crew until it's dealt with.

Delta Flyer options: in Juggernaut, Child's Play and One Small Step you can now send the Delta Flyer. In Juggernaut it cuts the crafting time and makes the away mission easier, and in One Small Step it lets you skip part 2.
The U.S.S. Equinox, remastered: in the Equinox chapter the Equinox uses its new, more detailed model, and in battle it fires its phaser banks and launches torpedoes.
The main menu's New Game button is now called New Campaign.
Potential finds: PoI events may now preview the items, crew and resources you might find.
Clearer PoI options: options with only one possible outcome no longer show a max marker.
Hero abilities: combat ability texts now read "Name: description" on every screen. The Hero Overview marks heroes that need a DLC.
Research reports no longer switch you to the side view.
Trades: when your cargo space runs short, the Aeroshuttle Bay trade button shows how much you'll actually receive.
Rewards: reward events that give two items now list each item on its own line.
Subtitles: cutscene subtitles now show long lines correctly, and the subtitle font is bigger.
Combat: auto-resolve is calculated from maximum hull. Several ships now fire from more weapon positions.
Waste Disassembler: Level 1 now produces 80 Deuterium (was 60) and 8 Duranium (was 6). Level 2 produces 120 Deuterium (was 80), 12 Duranium (was 8) and 8 Tritanium (was 6).
Bussard Collector: Level 1 now produces 5 (was 4), Level 2 produces 10 (was 8).
Tech costs: Warp Core Efficiency techs now also cost Dilithium, and hull techs now also cost Duranium.
Trade Protocols: the trade bonus is now +20% (was +15%).
Aeroshuttle Bay trades: almost all offers improved, and a few that were too good (mostly Science Point trades) were toned down.
Morale: injured and sick crew lower morale 20% less.
Species 8472: the damage they take from phasers has been reduced to fit the lore.
Resources: resources are spread more evenly, later sectors have less Duranium and Tritanium, and the Scorpion sector has a little more Deuterium and Duranium.

PoIs: Borg Cube Debris Field and Destroyed Borg Cube have more possible locations and appear more often in the Scorpion sector. Toxic Junkyard and the disease distress signal are more likely in Tomorrow's Yesterday, and planet-specific PoIs appear a little less often.
Dreadnought PoI: swapped excellent and good outcome types for one option at the end, because the good one was better.
Phenomena: adjusted the spawn rate of spatial phenomena in the second half of the campaign.
Night and Eye of the Needle: mission PoIs now disappear correctly after the mission.
To Eat or to Empty: added the missing wait time and quest tracker text, and the event now checks whether Kes is available.
Fixed quest progress issues in Infinite Regress, the Endgame and the Nothing Human PoI.
The Tuvix bridge dialogue no longer plays at the start of the sector.
Caretaker and Old Friends, New Enemies: PoIs keep the right visibility when you continue a game.
Mission PoIs (e.g. in Night) are visible again in saves from older versions.
Final Warning can always be triggered, and the cooldowns of the morale quests were improved.
The second mutiny step now leads to game over when morale drops to 0.
Latent Image no longer starts when the Doctor isn't on the ship.
Borg Cube Debris Field and Destroyed Borg Cube PoIs can appear again in sectors 6–12.
Away mission failures are no longer shown as successes, and away mission results no longer show negative XP.
PoI options that need a shuttle now only count shuttles in an active shuttle bay.
Hull damage shown in events now matches the damage you take, including the Reactive Armor reduction.
The combat room level now increases your weapon damage.
Researching Warp Core Efficiency now updates the cycle counter right away.
The Main Deflector no longer shows as offline while it's being upgraded, and the next-cycle preview is correct when you switch rooms on or off.
Techs that are unlocked from the start grant their items again (e.g. Borg nanites in the level 2 bio lab).
Crew conditions now create one combined report instead of one report per crew member.
Deactivated room widgets now scroll when there isn't enough space.
The gel pack description now correctly says Duranium instead of Tritanium.
The morale overview now updates right away when happiness changes.
The charge bar shows again while you hold to upgrade or dismantle a room, and the mouse indicator resets when you move off a room.
Fixed lighting in the Observation Lounge and the Aeroshuttle Bay, and clipping in a Borg room.
Dark Frontier: the Borg probe no longer surrenders.
Voyager no longer appears inside PoIs.
Fixed star systems with several stars but no inner planets, and missing shadows in single-star systems.
Dark Frontier: Voyager no longer shrinks away during the transwarp cutscene.
Phaser fire in cutscenes no longer disappears at long distances.
Controller navigation into the sector saves now works even without a Sector 1 save.
Custom difficulty can now be set with a gamepad.
Fixed navigation on the restart sector button.
The tech tree and enter ship buttons in the research info are no longer swapped.
The chance bar shows again for PoI choices with a fixed outcome.
Carey's ability name no longer appears twice in the Hero Overview.
The DLC store buttons now work more than once, even without the Steam overlay.
Fixed the spelling of the Energy Dissipator.
Fixed a crash when continuing a game after going back to the main menu.
Fixed a possible crash when going back to the main menu.
A save that fails to load no longer affects the next new game.
The German voice-over for Nunez's personal logs plays again.
The description of the First Performance selection is now translated.
Corrected a line of text in Counterpoint.
See you in the Delta Quadrant, Captains!
gameXcite & Daedalic Entertainment
Heyho everyone,
As we are constantly reading your feedback, this small hotfix tackles the
"reloading a savefile if a battery is turned on will turn of life support"- issue you mentioned in the forums and discord (together with minor visual adjustments, for example in 2 cutscenes).
We wish you ongoing save travels through the Delta Quadrant!
Heyho Captains!
We have a plethora of new bits and pieces for you in this new Update (1.7)! Most prominently, the long awaited Delta Flyer!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748013/e4fd5efd5d980ab786861ae1dbd15bded9440ec2.png"]

Built in the Shuttlebay, the Delta Flyer brings a brand-new questline with Tom Paris in Sector 7, construction mechanics, and a combat ally role that won't split your rewards. There are also new Delta Flyer-specific branches in several existing quests, including "Old Friends, New Enemies", "The Drone", and "Uprising".

Beyond the Delta Flyer, 1.7 is a hefty quality-of-life and stability pass - overhauled bridge UI, PlayStation gamepad support, a wave of quest fixes across some of the game's bigger storylines, and a bunch of crash and save game fixes.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748013/52ed92d7344834fe28a14536f3fc25f2ef259c8b.png"]
Console players will have to wait a little longer, as (unfortunately) is usually the case - the patch is coming to consoles in early June.
PS: (While we are at it - Are you at FedCon? We are! So come around and say "Hi!" and chat a bit about the game)

notes.title: And now for something completely different

items.text: I already said, you guys are crazy - but I wasn't even beginning to understand how crazy... You downloaded the Demo over 100.000 times in less than a week!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748013/264dd587c924e0e121f336431ad9255c9860ac44.png"]

The whole team is so thankful for the warmest welcome we could have wished for! Eventhough we want to make it right for everyone, we know for sure that some expectations won't be met. Being open with what the game is really about is crucial because of that, which is why we want to add one more answer to one of the most frequent questions going around (All information will be summarized in a general FAQ soon):
How free can I be in Star Trek: Voyager - Across the Unknown?

The overall premise of the game is to not just relive the ship's and the crew's story from the TV Series - but to make it your own. This said, the game is no sandbox with almost unlimited possibilities - we are still a small indie developer, that can't really pull this weight. But what you can expect though, is consequences of your own decisions pulling through each of your playthroughs, making them unique in themselves - even when encountering some fixpoints in the story. How you deal with them is up to you - every time anew.
Best Regards

Captain's Log, stardate 000.4 after the emergence of the Demo,

First off, let me start by saying - you guys are crazy! We knew that the Star Trek community is a very strong and dedicated one - but the positive feedback, congratulations and especially review score (and amount) that has come our way on various platforms is just flabbergasting!
Obviously there are still open questions, bugs or important wishes that you have brought up, which we are now concentrating on tackling.
This patch for the Demo, that we will be testing one more time over the weekend and plan to implement on Monday, will contain following fixes and adjustments:
Implemented hardware cursor
Fixed several rich text formatting issues
Added combat voice-overs
Replaced Talaxian Character for the quarterless shipmanagement quest - so no more confusion with Neelix!
Additionally to those first fixes, we want to answer some of the most burning questions that have been repeated basically everywhere, by everyone:

The demo is a pre-release version and we always planned on delivering some form of VO in the full release. But - as you can imagine, with a text-heavy game like ours it would not be very feasible to have a 100% Full VO, especially for an Indie-Studio. Right now we are looking into finding a worthy solution.
TL;DR; The final game will have partial VO. More information to follow.

The sound effects are not yet final. Legally it is not possible for us to “just copy” the existing sounds from the show (or the internet) and there is no official, digital library for them available - but we are looking at the moment into replicating them as identical as possible. We will keep you updated here as well on how well this works out.
While the demo is only in English, the full version will be localized into more languages including German, French, Spanish, Italian, Polish, Russian and Chinese.
Thanks again for your overwhelmingly positive and warm welcome into the huge Star Trek Family - we are looking forward to giving this sentiment back to you with a great 1.0 Release!
Best Regards,
gameXcite & Daedalic Entertainment
